prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer looking steeply downward while walking through a doorway (frame 1) into a room with partitions and a floor ~1.5–1.7 m below, then turning left (frames 2–3) and approaching a desk and a second person standing in a lab coat (frames 4–5). The wearer's own hands, forearms, and lower torso at the bottom of the frame are brightest (~0.3–0.6 m away), holding a small plastic bag within immediate reach, while the partition on the right in frame 3 passes within ~0.5–0.8 m and the containers on the floor to the left sit at ~1.5 m. Across frames 4 and 5, the desk surface (~0.8–1.2 m away) and the second person (~1.2–1.5 m ahead and to the right, facing toward the desk and camera wearer with their head cropped out of the top of the frame) grow brighter as the wearer approaches to within arm's reach of the desk edge and ~0.5 m of the other person's outstretched left hand. This map clarifies the 3D vertical separation between the raised desk surface, the monitor stand rising toward the camera in frame 5, and the recessed floor behind the desk, which flatten together in the overhead RGB view. However, the depth map is unreliable on the glossy floor ahead in frames 1–3, where specular reflections and dark regions render as near-black drop-offs, and on the transparent plastic bag, which blends into the depth of the wearer's hands and floor behind it.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates foreground actors and discrete objects from the room layout, detecting the camera wearer's hands and lower body at the bottom center (~0.3–0.6 m away) across all five frames and a second person at the upper right (~1.2–1.5 m away, ~0.8–1.0 m from the wearer's extended right hand) in frames 4 and 5. In frame 1, it labels the whiteboard on a rolling stand (~1.5–2.0 m ahead to the right) as a 'tv', while in frame 5 it locates a 'mouse' and 'keyboard' on the desk surface (~0.9–1.1 m away, to the left of the second person) that are within arm's reach of both the standing person and the approaching wearer. As the wearer walks forward and turns from the doorway toward the desk across frames 1–5, the second person enters the upper-right field of view with their torso angled toward the desk and their head occluded by the top frame boundary, while the desk monitor occludes part of the desk surface in frame 5. The map highlights small held and tabletop items that blend into the bright desk or floor in RGB, such as the document tray on the desk in frame 4 (labeled 'book') and the small plastic packet in the wearer's hands (labeled 'cell phone' in frame 3 and 'remote' in frame 4). However, it is heavily unreliable in its object classifications and completeness: it hallucinates a yellow floor sticker ~1.6 m below the camera as a 'sports ball' in frame 3, splits the wearer's own body into multiple 'person' instances in frame 4, and completely misses the desk, monitor, partitions, and floor containers.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks 2D hand and body keypoints against a black background, detecting only the camera wearer's own hands at the bottom center of frames 2, 3, and 4 (~0.3–0.5 m below and in front of the head-mounted camera) while leaving the surrounding room layout, furniture, and walls completely unrepresented. In frame 2, both the left and right magenta hand skeletons are clearly separated (~0.15 m apart) and oriented palms-inward as the fingers pinch the edges of the small plastic bag within immediate reach of the chest. In frame 3, the two hand skeletons converge at the bottom center as the fingers manipulate the bag, accompanied by a tangled cluster of yellow body keypoints overlaid on the left wrist, and by frame 4 only the left hand skeleton remains visible while the right hand (extended forward holding the bag at ~0.5 m) drops out of detection. Across the five-frame progression, the map captures the wearer's hands rising into view after frame 1 and separating as the right arm reaches toward the desk in frames 4–5, providing explicit finger joint articulations during two-handed manipulation that are partially self-occluded in the RGB image. However, the pose map is largely unreliable across the sequence: it fails to detect the wearer's hands in frames 1 and 5, misses the right hand in frame 4, collapses the wearer's body skeleton into a noisy fragment in frame 3, and completely fails to detect the second person standing ~1.2–1.5 m away behind the desk in frames 4 and 5 whose head is out of view.
